resultDetails.itemNameEn: Check whether the OS user passwords of all nodes have expired.
resultDetails.course: opsadmin user normal, left days : , expire date: 2025-01-08
resultDetails.itemSuggestCh: 1. Log in to the ManageOne Maintenance Portal and switch to the Service OM page. Choose Services > Resource > Compute Resource from the service list. Click the VM tab and locate the faulty node in the list. 3. Click VNC login and use the password of the root user to log in to the faulty node. 4.  Run the following command to check whether the password of OS account opsadmin has expired: chage -l opsadmin The command output is as follows: Last password change     : May 12, 2020Password expires     : Aug 10, 2020Password inactive     : Sep 09, 2020Account expires      : neverMinimum number of days between password change  : 0Maximum number of days between password change  : 90Number of days of warning before password expires : 15 The value of Password expires is the password expiration time of the opsadmin user. If the value is never, the password of the account never expires. If the value is another value, the password expires, and this workaround needs to be performed. 5. If the password expiration time of the opsadmin account is earlier than the current time, run the following command: passwd -x 90 opsadmin The command output is as follows: Adjusting aging data for the opsadmin user.passwd: Success
resultDetails.itemSuggestEn: 1.  Log in to the OperationCenter management page, go to the Service OM page, and choose Computing Resources from the service list. 2.  Click the VM tab and locate the faulty node in the list. 3.  Click VNC in the Operation column of the faulty node and use the password of user root to log in. 4.   Run the following command to check whether the password of OS account opsadmin has expired: chage -l opsadminhe command output is as follows: Last password change: May 12, 2020Password expires: Aug 10, 2020Password inactive: Sep 09, 2020Account expires: neverMinimum number of days between password change: 0Maximum number of days between password change: 90Number of days of warning before password expires: 15 In the command output, the value of Password expires is opsadmin's password expiration time. The value never indicates that the password of the opsadmin account never expires. Other values indicate that the password of the opsadmin account has an expiration time. In this case, perform the workaround. 5. If the password expiration time of user opsadmin is earlier than the current time, run the following command: passwd -x 90 opsadminhe following information is displayed: Adjusting aging data for user opsadmin. passwd: Success

resultDetails.itemNameEn: Check the CPU usage of a CBH service node.
resultDetails.descEn: The check is passed. The average CPU usage within 15 minutes does not exceed 85%.
resultDetails.course: Node cpuUseage:17.3% Less Than Threshold, Threshold:85.0%
resultDetails.itemSuggestCh: 1. Use PuTTY to log in to the faulty service node as the opsadmin user. 2.  Switch to the root user. sudo su3. Enter the password of the root user and press Enter when the following information is displayed. [sudo] password for root:4. Run the following command to check whether the CPU usage exceeds 85%.
resultDetails.itemSuggestEn: 1. Use PuTTY to log in to the faulty service node as user opsadmin.  2.  Run the following command to switch to user root:  sudo su3.  When the following information is displayed, enter the password of user root and press Enter:  Password:4.  Run the following command to check whether the current CPU usage exceeds 85%.5.  Run the kill -9 PID command to stop the process whose CPU usage is high (for example, greater than 15%). op -b -n16.  Wait for about 5 minutes and check whether the current CPU usage exceeds 15%.   o No: No further action is required.    o Yes: Go to 7. 7.  Contact Huawei technical support engineers.
